newsitem.title: USA: New York students hold funeral for research chimp.
newsitem.headline: New York students hold funeral for research chimp.

text.p: About 50 New York University students held a mock funeral Wednesday for Jello, a chimpanzee who was used in lab tests, then sent to a controversial facility in New Mexico where he died last month.
Students sang about stopping animal testing as the grim reaper stood next to a fake coffin containing a gorilla suit wearing a chimp face mask. A nearby banner read: "Jello R.I.P 1985-1997.'

NYU's Medical Centre and research chimpanzees in general have been the focus of controversy lately as researchers grapple with the idea they have bred too many chimpanzees in captivity than they have use for.

Animal rights activists want the animals retired to a preserve, but they say they would settle for a research programme that humanely handled the animals, many of whom have been infected with the HIV virus.
They have taken up the case of Jello's death because they say it is indicative of the facilities at the Coulston Foundation in New Mexico.
"They're just being condemned to death when they're sent to Coulston," said Olga Boshart, an NYU senior.
Chadwick Bovee, director of the Wetlands Preserves Animal Rights Action Team, said that Jello, an 11-year-old male chimp died because of negligent medical treatment.
"Jello's death is tragic, but it's really no surprise," Bovee said. "NYU should expect more animals to die."
The foundation denied any wrongdoing in the death.
A spokesman for the NYU Medical Centre, Dan Perkes, said that the university has sent about 100 chimps to Coulston and has about 100 left.
